subject: POC kickoff: traffic inventory & playbook for Borealis Health
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha.menon@borealishealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff: traffic inventory & playbook for Borealis Health

Thanks again for the time this morning, Asha — good alignment on goals. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan.

High-level objective
- Evaluate Redwood Inference on your clinical summarization and triage pipelines for a 6-week POC. Primary goals: latency/throughput SLOs, quality parity with current baseline, and cost per 1M tokens estimate under realistic traffic.

Scope (what we will run in POC)
- Inference routes: clinical-note summarization (primary), patient question-answering (secondary).
- Models: 1 LLM baseline (open model you prefer) + 1 Redwood-recommended quantized variant for cost testing.
- Environment: VPC/private deployment preferred (per your compliance note).

Traffic & workload data we need from Borealis (please share samples where possible)
- Baseline sustained RPS: expected sustained requests/sec during business hours.
- Burst patterns: expected peak RPS and duration (e.g., occasional 5–10 minute bursts).
- Concurrency: typical simultaneous open sessions / parallel requests.
- Token distribution: avg input tokens, avg output tokens, 90th / 99th percentile lengths, and max observed input tokens.
- Payloads: representative JSONL (no PHI; pseudonymized or synthetically generated is fine).
- Any transformations (token prefixes, templating, multi-turn context).

Success criteria (initial proposal)
- Latency: p95 response time < 350 ms for summarization route at baseline sustained load.
- Throughput: sustain baseline RPS for 6+ hours; handle peak bursts with graceful degradation (fallback model available).
- Quality: human eval on 50 seeded prompts — >=85% parity vs current baseline (we'll define rubric together).
- Cost: extrapolated cost per 1M tokens within 20% of target budget you provide.

Owners & roles
- Borealis: Asha (POC lead) — provide traffic samples, whitelist IPs, approve data handling.
- Redwood: Vanessa (eng/sales owner) — overall run coordination and timelines; Sean — infra sizing & deployment; Rafael — eval harness & quality measurement.

Proposed timeline
- By 2026-10-08: Borealis provides sample traffic JSONL and preferred model targets.
- 2026-10-12: kickoff tech run & capacity planning (30–45 min).
- 2026-10-13 to 2026-11-23: 6-week POC window (config, run, eval checkpoints week 2/4/6).

Immediate asks (for the next 72 hours)
1) Sample traffic file (pseudonymized) + a short note on token lengths and peak windows.
2) Confirmation that VPC/private deployment is required (you mentioned this on the call).
3) Any procurement contacts for DPA/contract paperwork (we can pre-share Redwood DPA template).

Attachments: I attached a short POC playbook (poc-playbook-v1.pdf) that lays out milestones and what Redwood will measure. Also referenced the Drive folder with artifact templates.

If that looks good I’ll schedule the capacity planning slot with Sean and Rafael for Oct 12.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: POC kickoff: traffic inventory & playbook for Borealis Health

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the clear recap and playbook. Confirming a few items and adding the immediate traffic numbers we have today (high level). I attached a sanitized sample file (borealis-traffic-samples.jsonl) to this reply.

Quick answers / numbers from our side
- Baseline sustained RPS (business hours): 5–8 RPS for the summarization endpoint.
- Typical concurrency: ~30 simultaneous sessions that can fan out to ~40 parallel requests during busy windows.
- Peak bursts: we see spikes to ~70–80 RPS for 2–5 minutes several times/day (batch exports kick off).
- Token distribution (sanitized): avg input ~180 tokens, avg output ~220 tokens, p90 input ~420, max observed input ~4,096 tokens (rare).
- Data sensitivity: this dataset is clinical; we will require VPC/private deployment and SOC2 evidence.

Timeline & next steps
- We can deliver a properly sanitized sample by EOD 2026-10-08.
- Legal: I’ll loop in procurement next — they need the DPA and a short vendor security packet.
- Plan: Oct 12 kickoff works for us; can do 10:00–10:45 PT.

One clarification: when you describe "sustain baseline RPS for 6+ hours" — our baseline window is typically 9a–5p ET. We want to make sure the POC simulates full-day patterns.

I’ll review the playbook and confirm procurement contacts in my next email.

Thanks,
Asha Menon
Director, Product — Clinical AI
Borealis Health
asha.menon@borealishealth.com

Thanks — looping Rafael and Priyom so infra & eval are aligned. A few quick notes from the infra side after reading Asha's numbers:

Technical considerations / initial sizing thoughts
- Sustained 5–8 RPS with 30–40 concurrency and 70–80 RPS short bursts likely maps to small pool of GPU-backed hosts + autoscale by a warm standby pool.
- For the initial POC I recommend two GPU nodes (A100 class) with a small on-demand pool to absorb bursts. We’ll instrument continuous batching and prefix caching to lower per-token costs.
- Max input tokens ~4k: we need to confirm tokenization (model-specific) — larger contexts increase KV cache size and memory. Rafael: can you estimate memory footprint for the two candidate models?

Questions for Asha (quick)
1) Can the sample JSONL include timestamp fields so we can reconstruct burst windows?
2) Do you expect multi-turn context to be sent each call, or will the client only send the latest prompt and rely on server-side stored session context?

I’ll prep a rough cost/size estimate and bring to the Oct 12 capacity call.

- Sean
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com

Perfect — thanks Asha and team. I uploaded a slightly edited POC playbook into the Drive folder (poc-playbook-v1.pdf) and attached a DPA template and the sample traffic file you sent for our test harness.

Updated owners & checkpoints (v1)
- Borealis (Asha): deliver sanitized traffic + procurement contact by 2026-10-08.
- Redwood infra (Sean): capacity plan + initial cluster suggestion by 2026-10-11.
- Redwood eval (Rafael & Priyom): evaluate quality metrics and assemble 50-seed prompt set by 2026-10-11.
- Joint: Tech kickoff 2026-10-12 10:00 PT (calendar invite to follow).

Measurement plan (how we'll judge success)
- Latency: p95 under 350 ms at baseline RPS (measured over 8-hour window).
- Resilience: burst handling with <10% error rate during 70–80 RPS spikes.
- Quality: >85% pass rate on human-eval rubric across 50 prompts.
- Cost: per-day run cost reported and extrapolated to per-1M tokens.

Deliverables to expect from Redwood after kickoff
1) Infra config (node types, batch settings, expected utilization).
2) Eval harness with seed prompts and scoring rubric.
3) Weekly run reports (latency, throughput, error rate, sample outputs).

Asha — can you confirm procurement contact and whether we should route DPA through your legal or procurement inbox? Once I have that contact I’ll share the DPA and the brief security packet.

Thanks everyone — I’ll send the calendar invite for Oct 12 shortly.
